title: Component Playground & Migration Cheat Sheet for Primitives
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a compact, reusable 'Component Playground' page in the design docs that bundles interactive examples, canonical usage patterns, and a one-page migration cheat sheet for primitives (Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts). The goal is to reduce developer/PM/design confusion when upgrading to the new token set and component APIs: provide code snippets, do/don't micro-examples, visual reference of edge cases, and a step-by-step migration checklist. This ticket covers content authoring, Figma embed wiring, example story extraction, and a short engineering README for the component library owners to adopt the page in the docs site.
acceptance_criteria: Playground page exists in docs with embedded live examples for Button, Table, Chart, and Token inspector.
Each component example includes: usage snippet (TSX/HTML), props table, accessibility notes, and a do/don't micro-example.
Migration Cheat Sheet: mapped old token names to new tokens + 5 common migration snippets for Buttons and Tables.
Design review completed and sign-off from UX (Marta Silva) and PM (Devon Park).
Engineering integration guide (README) with links to story files and a sample GitHub PR for adoption.
Automated smoke check (visual diff) added to the docs pipeline referencing the example stories.
migration_notes: High-level: aim for non-breaking CSS variables where possible; prefer token aliases for backwards compat.
Tokens mapping (common): OLD: --rdw-primary -> NEW: --rwd-token-primary-500; OLD: --rdw-muted -> NEW: --rwd-token-neutral-200.

Buttons: replace variant prop
  - old: <Button kind="primary"> -> new: <Button tone="brand" size="md">
  - provide migration helper in stories: use mapButtonKind(oldKind) utility in migration helper PR.
Tables: default row height increased; migration checklist includes adjusting custom cell paddings, verifying sticky header behavior, and testing keyboard nav for large datasets.
Charts: ensure color tokens are mapped; update legend spacing token to new scale (spacing-3 -> spacing-6).
Rollback path: provide fallback CSS that maps old token names to new tokens for 1 release cycle; document code snippet for platform teams.
examples: Button (do): <Button tone="brand">Save</Button> — use semantic tones not arbitrary colors.
Button (don't): <button style="background:#0066FF;color:white"> — avoid inline color styling; use tokens.
Table (do): use <Table virtualized> for >1000 rows; include aria-rowcount and rowindex attributes.
Chart (do): use colorScale token set and provide high-contrast alternate for accessibility.
Token inspector: interactive palette showing token name, value, and example usage for each token family.
